nodes.summary: A set $S$ of natural numbers is recursively enumerable if and only if it is Diophantine, that is, there is a polynomial $p$ with integer coefficients such that $n \in S$ exactly when $p(n, t_1, \dots, t_k) = 0$ for some natural numbers $t_1, \dots, t_k$.
nodes.title: Davis–Putnam–Robinson–Matiyasevich theorem

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi : A \to R$ be a ring homomorphism of commutative rings, with $R$ nontrivial. For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the empty subset of $R^k$ is Diophantine over $R$ with coefficients from $A$ through $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The empty set is Diophantine

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi : A \to R$ be a ring homomorphism of commutative rings. A subset $S \subseteq R$ is Diophantine over $R$ with coefficients from $A$ through $\varphi$ when the set $\{(s) : s \in S\} \subseteq R^1$ of one-coordinate points with coordinate in $S$ is a Diophantine subset of $R^1$ over $R$ with coefficients from $A$ through $\varphi$.
nodes.title: Diophantine subsets of a ring

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi : A \to R$ be a ring homomorphism of commutative rings. For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the whole space $R^k$ is Diophantine over $R$ with coefficients from $A$ through $\varphi$.
nodes.title: The whole space is Diophantine

nodes.summary: Let $\varphi : A \to R$ be a ring homomorphism of commutative rings and let $k \in \mathbb{N}$. Polynomials with coefficients in $A$ are evaluated at points with coordinates in $R$ by first mapping their coefficients into $R$ by $\varphi$.
